newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Bangladesh Newspapers - Sept 18.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Bangladesh press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Dick Cheney, former U.S. defence secretary and chief of the oil giant Halibarton, is due to arrive Dhaka on Friday to discuss investment of $100 million in oil/gas exploration in the Bay of Bengal.
Thirtysix percent of vehicles plying on the streets of Dhaka and other main cities were found emiting black smoke and other exhausts injurious to health.

The main opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has decided to take to the street against the government. The decision was taken at the BNP standing committee meeting yesterday at the official residence of party chief Begum Khaleda Zia.

Ten students were injured in a clash between student activists of the ruling Awami League and rival Jamaat-e-Islami at Chittagong University. Also in Chittagong, a Jamaat-e-Islami worker was shot dead by armed cadres of a rival party.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said her first official visit to China and talks with Chinese leaders were "very positive and fruitful."
Some 55 percent of 9.3 million population of Dhaka city are living below the poverty line, an Asian Development Bank study said.
International Development Association (IDA) is expected to lend Bangladesh $105 million for its Poverty-alleviation Micro-finance Project.
The Nomura International Plc, an investment banking arm of the Nomura Securities Company Ltd, has shown interest to invest in Bangladesh.

Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina has given the go-ahead to investigate corruption charges against former prime minister Begum Khaleda Zia. Meanwhile, the Anti-Corruption bureau has filed cases against the son and brother Khaleda Zia and three other former ministers on charges of misappropriation of government funds, corruption and misuse of power. -- Dhaka Newsroom 880-2-506363
